explanation:
[EFFECT]
Weather has a clear step-like effect on predicted hourly bike rentals. Clear skies (category 1) give demand a small positive boost (+0.047 in log contribution), while mist or cloudy conditions (category 2) leave demand almost completely unchanged (−0.002, essentially neutral). The real drop comes with precipitation: light rain or snow (category 3) suppresses demand by roughly −0.35 in log space — the largest single penalty — and heavy rain (category 4) also suppresses demand strongly (−0.26), only slightly less so than light rain/snow.

[IMPORTANCE]
`weathersit` ranks **6th out of 9 features** with an importance score of 0.061. It sits in the middle of the pack — well below the dominant factors of hour-of-day (0.889), temperature (0.253), year (0.217), month (0.086), and humidity (0.083), but still meaningfully more influential than weekday, wind speed, and holiday.

[RECOMMENDATION]
When rain or snow is forecast, the model predicts a substantial drop in demand, so consider pre-emptively reducing bike-rebalancing effort and staffing at stations during those hours to avoid unnecessary operational costs.
